headline: Multi-omic QTL and Mendelian randomization nominate candidate disease genes
label: Integrative Genetic Target Prioritization
summary: Fine-mapping, colocalization and single-cell and tissue-specific QTL resources are narrowing variant-to-gene candidates for complex disease.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of genetic association data as a filter for candidate gene identification. Mendelian randomization, frequently paired with colocalization or SMR against mQTL, eQTL and pQTL data, recurs across the set. Examples include the Alzheimer's study prioritizing 46 druggable genes from brain sc-eQTL data and the adenomyosis study linking seven exosome-related genes to risk. A newer feature is the pairing of these causal-inference filters with cell-type and tissue-level resolution: the mV2G atlas integrates 24 functional genomic evidence types across 50 tissues, CT-FM and CT-FM-SNP infer independent causal cell types and candidate variants, and the bipolar disorder TWAS prioritizes HSPE1 with immune cell-specific regulatory evidence. Other items rely on GWAS-based cTWAS with AlphaGenome prediction or Basenji deep-learning predictions, so the thread is dominant rather than universal.
